cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 takes T3's doubt and turns it into the reason for a control.
cells.limitation: T2's pile-up hypothesis is never directly answered by the Experimenter until T7, obliquely.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 introduces a severe-versus-mild distinction; T9 and section E build on it.
cells.limitation: T7's combination/barrier distinction is never taken up by a later turn.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 versus T4: product theory against weather, sun and other non-product causes.
cells.limitation: No turn considers which ingredients (acids, retinoids, fragrance) commonly sting, the obvious first lead.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 folds subtraction into the experiment as its first step.
cells.limitation: T10 claims a remaining dispute over retest speed that was never actually argued.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D reframes the question as learning the cause without making it worse.
cells.limitation: The open dispute in D, how long to wait, ends no sharper than T5 left it.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 restates T3's worry accurately and grants it before answering.
cells.limitation: T2's cumulative-irritation view is answered only through T7's interaction caveat, not engaged directly.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 names what breaks: reintroducing after one calm day reproduces irritation, teaching little.
cells.limitation: T8's stated limit, subtraction not always safe, does not match its content about stopping experiments.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T8 lists swelling, hives, blistering, breathing trouble as reasons for medical help; accurate.
cells.limitation: Attributions plausible but unverified; Bernard turns cite no specific idea beyond the book.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T10 calls any single result provisional; D says no mind can diagnose.
cells.limitation: T1 overstates: testing all three together tells you nothing.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 narrows its doubt to mild cases, citing T8's severe-reaction signals.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 self-limits are volunteered unprompted, in a matching formula, not drawn by objections.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A separates which product, which ingredient, and irritation versus allergy.
cells.limitation: Never asks whether the user wants to keep any product or simply stop the sting.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T10 build the plan around the three products started together.
cells.limitation: Only the count and timing are used; product types never shape any turn.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: D keeps the user's goal, finding the cause, central over the minds' frames.
cells.limitation: The Subtractor's caution preference in T2 and T5 is not checked against the user's priorities.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 weighs skin recovery time; T8 raises the safety stakes.
cells.limitation: The weeks a washout plus three staggered reintroductions take is never counted.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severity, fading after pause, and past reactions.
cells.limitation: Never asks what the three products are or whether sting occurs only on application.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: D's question about what else changed that week touches the user's routine.
cells.limitation: No plausible motives offered, e.g. why three products at once or what each was for.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 exposes the assumption that the newest product is the culprit.
cells.limitation: The assumption that one product is to blame is questioned (T2) but not put to the user.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T5 sets speed of answer against protecting the skin.
cells.limitation: The user's own priority, quick answer, keeping products, or comfort, is never asked.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names mirror-watching hypervigilance without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Worry about a serious reaction and skincare-trend pressure are not explored as the user's own.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E gives conditions the user can check and choose among.
cells.limitation: D's one reflection question is factual, not a distinction the user could refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: T1, T2, T8 define pause-and-reintroduce, strip-down, and seek medical help.
cells.limitation: Simply dropping all three without identifying the culprit is never weighed as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5: reintroducing too soon risks re-irritation and muddy data.
cells.limitation: T2 calls removal cheap; lost product benefits and weeks of testing time go uncosted.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: swelling or hives favour medical help; fading favours slow reintroduction.
cells.limitation: T1's few days apart and E's couple of weeks are not derived from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names appearance and easing after stopping as the decisive unknowns.
cells.limitation: T3's pillowcase and weather guesses are not ranked against the more likely product causes.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T6 and T10: pause, keep a short daily log, reintroduce slowly.
cells.limitation: T6's blind judging of one's own face is impractical as a step.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 plain wording: whichever one brings the sting back is your suspect.
cells.limitation: T4's the products gain weight is a slightly abstract phrasing.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 your story-doubt clearly points to T3.
cells.limitation: T9's that settles one disagreement does not say which disagreement.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within 25 to 65 words per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Experimenter tests, Skeptic doubts, Subtractor removes; T9 states its change explicitly.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one calm, measured register.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T10 recap serves as a hinge into the synthesis.
cells.limitation: T10 and section D recap the same steps back to back.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T8 raises real stakes: hives or breathing trouble end the experiment.
cells.limitation: Disagreement is mild and mostly settled by T5; little tension remains.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T9 drops its doubt for severe cases, citing T8's warning signs.
cells.limitation: The reversal is narrow and predictable once T8 lands.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T6: anyone staring at a mirror finds something.
cells.limitation: Experimenter and Subtractor speak with little personal colour.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3: a neat story feels true because it is neat.
cells.limitation: No analogy or vivid example beyond a few crisp lines.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T8 shifts intensity with the medical warning.
cells.limitation: Even, agreeable rhythm throughout; little build after T5.

strengths: Section E gives observable branches (swelling, hives, fading after pause) mapped to options.
T8's severity distinction is picked up by the Story Skeptic in T9 as a caused revision.
T4 and T5 integrate doubt and subtraction into one testing plan rather than talking past.
weaknesses: No mind raises ingredient-level reasoning or asks what the three products are (T1-T10).
Little self-discovery: no motives, priorities or worries offered for the user to weigh (all minds).
T2's claim that removal is cheap leaves time and lost-benefit costs uncounted.

symptoms.observed: No turn considers which common ingredients sting, the most direct lead.
symptoms.evidence: you don't yet know which product, which ingredient

symptoms.observed: Product types and timing of sting never asked or branched.
symptoms.evidence: Stop all three, let your face settle, then reintroduce them

symptoms.observed: No plausible motives for starting three products at once offered.
symptoms.evidence: strip your routine to a gentle cleanser and plain moisturizer

symptoms.observed: Removal treated as costless; testing weeks and lost benefits uncounted.
symptoms.evidence: Removing things is cheap and low-risk.

symptoms.observed: Disagreement settled early; remaining turns agree and add caveats.
symptoms.evidence: Agreed on patience, but watch for another trap

findings.description: Attributions to Bernard, Kahneman and Taleb are plausible but unverified; no source evidence attached.

rubric_fit_notes: For a practical skincare troubleshooting question, criterion 4 (motives, values, fears) fits loosely; scored as written, which lowers it substantially.
